correctness.rationale: For m>=2, an odd reduced linear coefficient cancels under a half-period translate. If it is even, the quadratic coefficient is odd, and the squared character sum has exactly two equal positive contributions, giving magnitude squared 2^{m+1}, so cannot vanish. At m=1 the sum equals 1+(-1)^{U+V}. Pairwise first-differing-bit orthogonality follows. An inductive branch-count capacity argument forces each full-size orthogonal frequency set to be a tree with a unique dyadic 1-Lipschitz low-map and one of four terminal edges per leaf. Converse is immediate from the same zero criterion. Counting bit functions gives 2^{2^k-2}, terminal choices 2^{2^k}; exact enumerations for N=2,4 and exhaustive tests of all predicted bases N=2,4,8 corroborate this universal proof, as does the all-coefficient exact cyclotomic zero check up to N=64.

value.rationale: This completes a natural characteristic-two family of finite parabola exponential-basis partner problems, complementing but not reducing to the published odd-prime theorem. The terminal branching supplies a meaningful structural obstruction to graph-only spectra, and the all-level exact closed count is a nontrivial invariant useful in Fourier sampling and spectral-set classification. The proof gives a generative description for every basis, not a small table or standard Gauss-sum restatement.
